When supported by the model, attachments remain multimodal content.
For a prompt-backed side's non-hidden declared relationships, runtimes inject the built-in lifecycle tools:
The `agent` argument of `subagent_create` / `subagent_message` enumerates relationship names.
Relationship configuration can map args to: initial user message (`initUserMessageProperty`) initial attachments (`initAttachmentsProperty`) human-readable child name (`initAgentNameProperty`)
only `nameEnv` and `descriptionEnv` are model-visible

Each `options.imports[specifier]` entry is a synthetic module whose namespace is a frozen copy of the host-provided object. The key `default` (when present) becomes that module's default export.
Each `options.modules[specifier]` entry is a source-backed ES module evaluated inside the sandbox.
Primitives (`string`, `number`, `boolean`, `null`, `undefined`, `bigint`) cross by value.
Plain objects, arrays, `Map`, `Set`, `Date`, typed arrays cross by structured clone (deep copy; no shared reference).
Functions cross as callable proxies. Calls forward serialized arguments and marshal the return value (awaiting any returned `Promise`) back.
The sandbox has its own microtask queue. `Promise`, `await`, and (at runtime discretion) `queueMicrotask` behave normally.
Top-level `await` is supported. A module "completes" once its top-level evaluation promise settles and the configured-export resolution ([§14.5](#145-configured-export-resolution)) finishes.
A hook decorates turns owned by something else — it runs around steps and messages, its failures are non-fatal to the decorated turn, and it may not own a side.
Hooks that run during active execution also receive [`state.execution`](/0.2.0/specification/threads/execution-state) with step counts, active dual-side, and abort signal context.
| `after_thread_created` | After thread creation, before execution | Initialize thread state |
| `after_subagent_created` | On parent after child thread creation | Track or initialize child relationships |
Thread hooks are scoped to the active parent composition rather than running globally.
Child before hooks — `before_parent` requirements from enabled direct child relationships, in side A then side B relationship order and child declaration order
Prompt-level hooks — A non-empty active prompt `hooks` array is the parent's base set
Agent-level hooks — If the prompt has no hooks, the agent's `hooks` array is the parent's fallback base set
Child after hooks — `after_parent` requirements (the default stage), in the same stable relationship/declaration order
If none of these sources declares a matching hook, no hook runs.
Downloaded or installed packages are not global hook sources.
At-rest operations have no active prompt. They resolve lifecycle hooks from the thread's agent-level `hooks` array.
All thread hooks receive a `ThreadState` instance as their first parameter and a `HookExecutionContext` as their final parameter.
Called after a message is successfully inserted. Cannot modify the message.
Called when a tool call starts — before the tool executes, while the model may still be generating the rest of the call.

When the tool declares a [`progressArgument`](/0.2.0/specification/tools#7-progress-reporting), the hook fires as soon as *just that argument* has finished streaming (not the whole call), passing its value as `progress`.
Called before a tool result is stored in the database.
Called after a tool executes successfully.
If hook returns `null`, the original result is used
If hook returns a result, it replaces the original
Called after a tool execution fails. Can return modified error or null for original.
Each thread owns an ordered, persistent list of messages

| `tool_calls` | `string \| null` | JSON-encoded array of tool calls. Each entry is `{ id: string, type: 'function', function: { name: string, arguments: string } }`, where `arguments` is itself JSON-encoded |
| `status` | `'pending' \| 'completed' \| 'failed' \| null` | Lifecycle state. `pending` while the message is queued or still being generated |

| `maxDepth` | `number` | - | Max nesting depth |
`role: 'user'` is the side B perspective — a message side A acts on.
`role: 'assistant'` is the side A perspective — a message side B acts on.
This mapping is independent of what backs each side (human, prompt, or handler).
Subagent traffic delivered to a parent lands in the perspective that prompts the relationship's *owning side* to take its turn
If the thread is executing, queued messages are injected before the next LLM request.
If the thread is idle, queueing forces a new turn.
Queued messages are processed in order.
Returns `true` if the message was found and removed, `false` otherwise.

A human on side A is legal.
`maxSessionTurns` is *optional on every agent shape*.
Exchange counting is uniform across backings: a handler turn counts like a prompt turn when a cap is set.

Both sides are explicit. There is no implicit "missing side B is a human" default
| `maxSessionTurns` | `number` | - | Session exchange safety cap ([§1.3](#13-derivations)) |
| `primary` | `boolean` | `true` | Whether the agent is a user-facing entry point. Clients omit non-primary agents from agent pickers. A non-primary agent remains addressable |

`AgentDefinition` also accepts optional packaging metadata — `packageName`, `version`, `author`, `license` — consumed only when the agent is packed for distribution.
`name`: tool that controls the lifecycle action
`messageProperty`: which arg field becomes lifecycle message text
`attachmentsProperty`: which arg field contains attachment path(s)
A handler-backed side's turn ends when its handler invocation returns
A human-backed side's turn ends when the human's inbound message is persisted.
When `exposeAsTool: true`, an agent referenced directly in a prompt's `tools` array is a handoff: the tool call transfers control of the *same thread* to the target agent, preserving history.
Handoff requires the target agent to have a human side matching the thread's conversational surface.
`exposeAsTool` + `toolDescription` are the composability contract — `toolDescription` is the default model-facing description when the agent is composed, and any agent may be composed.
Requirements apply only to direct parent relationships; they do not propagate transitively through the child graph.

`optional` relationships contribute hooks only while their flag is enabled. `hidden: true` affects model visibility, not composition, so hidden enabled relationships still contribute their required hooks.
Each requirement names a thread-scoped hook in the child's own package namespace. User-scoped hooks cannot be required on a parent.
The hook receives the parent's `ThreadState` and remains active for the lifetime of the enabled relationship. It applies during every prompt on either side of the parent.
Duplicate hook IDs within one child's `parentHooks` declaration are invalid.

When execution reaches the human-backed side's turn, the child session pauses: the child's registry status becomes `awaiting_human`, and the session resumes when a human's inbound message arrives on that side's perspective.
